scope: Public official sources and authorized repository code only.
limitations: No proprietary source code was recovered.
Product behavior does not establish a particular queue, prompt, memory algorithm, database schema, or exactly-once execution mechanism.
The absence of a feature from a public UI or document does not establish that an internal component is absent.
Per Pulse's globally continuous, locally activated, multi-timescale Context Body is a design requirement, not an inference that these reference products implement the same model.

sources.title: How We Designed Muse
sources.finding: Main and side chats, interruption, editable memory, background work, goals, approvals, and artifacts are public product behaviors.

sources.title: How We Built Safety Into Muse
sources.finding: The disclosed stack separates the agent runtime from host authorization, credential mediation, durable storage, and a browser broker; human takeover pauses agent control.

sources.title: Grok Bot overview
sources.finding: Named Bots retain their own conversations and working context while using shared account computer resources and cloud execution.

sources.title: Create and manage Bots
sources.short_excerpt: working context that develops over time
sources.finding: Role instructions persist; duplication copies configuration without copying learned memory or history; hiding and pausing have different effects.

sources.title: Message and collaborate
sources.finding: Direct user messages redirect ongoing work and receive priority. Asynchronous Bot messages can wake recipients; stopping does not undo completed effects.

sources.title: Use the computer and apps
sources.finding: Bots share files, authentication state, and plugins. Individual screens coordinate computer use without providing account isolation; durable and temporary environments differ.

sources.title: Skills and routines
sources.short_excerpt: The learned skill is a draft
sources.finding: Skills encode method, routines bind an owner and trigger, and demonstrations yield draft skills. Event integrations are distinct from ordinary plugins.

sources.title: Approvals, security, and privacy
sources.finding: Unattended approvals expire without execution after about ten minutes. Updating a future allow rule does not execute the expired action.

sources.title: Files and results
sources.finding: Artifact cards support inspection and revision; delegated results need a return path into the computer and conversation, not only intermediate shared files.

sources.title: Settings and notifications
sources.finding: Working, unread activity, and needs-attention states differ. Notification preferences and active device influence delivery and input-needed escalation.

sources.title: Grok Bot security
sources.finding: The documentation describes separate action review, backend-held connector tokens, and distinct admin audit and action recordings. Network restrictions and plugin restrictions differ.

sources.title: Manage Grok Bot computers
sources.finding: Recreation moves work at a safe point while retaining durable disk. Termination stops current work, and repeated administrative starts avoid duplicate operations.

sources.title: Security FAQ
sources.finding: The documented isolation unit is the user microVM, shared by that user's Bots. Persistent disk does not guarantee preserved or unexpired authentication sessions.

sources.title: Troubleshooting
sources.finding: Client disconnection does not necessarily stop cloud work. Input, approvals, login, quota, or unavailable screens can block progress; update and reset differ.

sources.title: Team Bots
sources.finding: Team memory and private conversations coexist. Computer and credential placement depends on the conversation: individual member context or a separate shared context.

contracts.contract: Acknowledge only durable input and retain its target context and admission result.
Persist a new intent revision, deliver it at a supported boundary, and preserve prior effects.
Project running and typed waiting reasons from authoritative execution records.
Bind dispatch to exact action, scope, authority, and canonical arguments; reconcile uncertain effects.
Return immutable source-linked versions through validated artifact handles.
Separate logical context ownership from physical resource exclusion and security isolation.
Recover durable state without treating missing effect receipts as safe replay.
Track evidence provenance and versions across observations, preferences, and derived summaries.
Carry parent ownership, acceptance criteria, stable delivery identity, and a return destination.
Turn bounded deduplicated triggers into ordinary native causal inputs.
Review, version, test, and activate a procedure independently of its recurrence.
Notify on meaningful results or needed input, with deduplication and acknowledgement.
Track generation, readiness, credentials, resource lease, human takeover, and safe migration.
Reserve before admission, settle usage idempotently, and retain unknown usage across restart.

code_findings.title: Shared workspace exclusion
code_findings.baseline: Physical replace validation and effect are separate; publication guard admits and drains without mutual exclusion.
code_findings.sprint_status: Process-local shared writer lane implemented for structured mutation, restore, and command execution; see final tests and implementation notes.
code_findings.caveat: Cooperating writers in one process only; no OS exclusion for external writers.

code_findings.title: Environment broker
code_findings.status: Add one useful broker-backed provider through existing Kernel authority

code_findings.title: Routine input adapter
code_findings.status: Reuse native causal admission instead of adding another runtime
